title: Tenant-quarantine sentinel and staggered upgrade automation for Private VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Private VPC customers require zero-surprise control plane upgrades. Current manual and ad-hoc canary promotion steps are error-prone when a tenant's runtime/topology drifts from our test corpus. We need an automated 'upgrade sentinel' workflow that quarantines a small tenant slice, performs a terraform plan+apply guarded by drift checks, runs a lightweight health probe suite, and either advances the cohort or aborts and creates rollbacks/alerts.
goals: 1) Implement an IaC-level sentinel that validates terraform plans against a tenant-specific compatibility matrix before applying. 2) A staged promotion engine that moves from 1% -> 10% -> 50% slices with automated health-gates. 3) Observable signals and auto-remediation playbooks for common failure classes. 4) Reusable terraform modules and runbook snippets for Private control plane upgrades.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sentinel service can fetch per-tenant compatibility rules and run terraform plan checks without applying.
- A tenant slice can be quarantined and upgraded in an isolated path with no impact to remaining tenants.
- Health-gates evaluate latency, error-rate, KV-cache hit ratio, and API contract regressions; if any gate trips, the system aborts promotion and initiates rollback automation.
- All upgrade attempts and final state are recorded in upgrade-audit buckets and surfaced in Console rollout view.
- Terraform modules include 'safety_mode' toggle and plan-diff export to storage for postmortems.
design_notes:
- Sentinel will be a lightweight controller that orchestrates: terraform plan -> plan-diff analyzer -> canary-apply (on isolated controlplane) -> canary-health-runner -> promotion controller.
- Use an opt-in tenant label 'upgrade-quarantine' injected via tenant metadata to limit blast radius.
- Plan diff analysis leverages schema contract tests + resource drift heuristics; flag changes to critical resources (RBAC, network) as high-severity.
- Promote via staged routing policy using tenant traffic-splits; traffic-split config lives in terraform and is patched by the sentinel on successful gates.
- Avoid central synchronous blocking: use event-driven state machine persisted in upgrades-postgres with idempotent step markers.
tradeoffs:
- Stronger plan gating increases false-block risk for complex customer topologies; we mitigate with 'allowlist' overrides with human approval.
- Running isolated controlplanes for canaries increases infra cost; to reduce expense we reuse burstable 'canary-pools' shared across tenants with fast teardown.
- Full spec validation is expensive; we focus checks on a curated subset of fields that historically cause regressions (network, auth, operator versions).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for plan-diff analyzer and gating rules.
- Integration tests using a seeded set of tenant manifests in a staging VPC (automated via pipeline).
- Chaos tests: inject latency and KV-cache corruption in canary controlplane to validate rollback.
- End-to-end dry-run where sentinel runs plan+analysis and emits signals without applying to validate detection heuristics.
observability:
- Add metrics: upgrade_attempts_total, upgrade_gate_failures{gate}, canary_latency_p50/p95, canary_error_rate.
- Emit structured events to Console: upgrade.started, upgrade.promoted, upgrade.aborted, upgrade.rollback.completed.
- Attach plan-diff artifact link and upgrade logs to the Console rollout timeline for triage.
failure_modes:
- False-positive gate triggers: provide manual override workflow and 'confidence window' where human approval required.
- Partial apply due to terraform timeouts: sentinel must detect incomplete state and trigger state-reconciliation job.
- Tenant-specific operator incompatibility: automatically pin previous operator image and mark tenant for remediation.
